warning for the upper elevations of the Haines Highway near Haines
Customs, and replaced with a winter weather advisory for the Klondike
Highway near White Pass.

possible.

* IMPACTS...Possibility for reduced visibilities due to blowing snow.

snow and reduce visibilities.

conditions where available call 511 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 8 at 12:26PM AKST until November 10 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between two and eight inches and ice accumulations around a light
glaze. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph, mainly across southern
parts of the Anchorage Hillside.

* WHERE...Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River.

* WHEN...From noon Monday to 3 PM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday evening and Tuesday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause damage to trees and power lines.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong storm system moving across the Gulf
of Alaska will bring a mix of snow, freezing rain and rain to much
of the Anchorage Hillside and Eagle River between Monday afternoon
and early Tuesday afternoon.  Precipitation will start as mainly
heavy snow by Monday afternoon, then transition to a mix of snow
and freezing rain late Monday night to early Tuesday morning as
east winds begin to pick up. Precipitation could transition to
plain rain by Tuesday morning as temperatures rise above freezing.
Uncertainty for the timing of precipitation type transition remains
high, with a later transition to rain and freezing rain potentially
leading to higher snowfall totals.

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering northerly swells generated by
distant surface low over the central Atlantic will support

properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
